newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Coffee mulls direction, cocoa licks wound.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Coffee mulls direction, cocoa licks wound.

text.p: March coffee volatilities spiked higher this week in an otherwise featureless trade for options after a dizzying price swing that blurred investors' views.
Traders said a spate of bids on March $1,600 calls squeezed up the vols to 42-43 percent, but May vols were steady around 38 percent with activity limited to straight puts and calls.
Cocoa was licking its wounds after a bear raid which slashed prices by five percent on Wednesday, shattering the market's upside prospects only days after a surge to 938 stg basis May.

While futures remained under siege by aggressive fund selling, cocoa players saw little point in dabbling in options, focusing instead on where the market might bottom out after a breach of contract lows.
"(Last week) there was underlying interest to buy the calls because the market looked pretty strong, then come this week and the interest disappeared," said one market maker.
Technical charts looked ghastly for buyers, but out-of-the-money calls remained the best strategy for building up a long portfolio on distant contacts, traders said.
Alternatively, investors could buy the futures and puts at the same time.
May 850 puts, a solid support level for the futures, appeared to be a good buy for bears but there was little interest.

"People don't believe in the downside and they don't want to spend money. It's all very good buying puts but if the market started to rally higher you've spent 20 quid (pounds sterling) on something which is worthless," said one.
Vols were subdued with May bid at 16 percent and offered at 20-22.

Demand for coffee options clustered around March $1,400 and $1,600 calls as players continued to square up positions and cover shorts amid a swathe of crop news from Brazil and Colombia that suggested a tight supply scenario for the near-term.
"What people are looking at is a couple of days consolidation before it takes another leg up," said one trader.
One recommended strategy for a protected upside was to sell March $1,400 puts and buy $1,500 calls for a premium of $10.

Some traders were using options for a one-to-one backing of futures sales to avoid being naked short. A few straddles also traded on Wednesday involving buying the $1,600 call and the $1,500 put for a two-way protection.

Coffee traders said the market's paltry volume during what is seen a consolidation process before a fresh upside break towards the $1,648 target meant roasters were still hesitant to commit themselves to a sizeable offtake.
May robusta could find support at around $1,495-$1,515 in the near term but some traders reckoned a breach of $1,450 could attract fund liquidation.
